title: A file API that does more than upload

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A file uploader that can also restart your Docker containers. That's SpringBootFilesUploader.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's a Kotlin REST API on Spring Boot. Its first job is in the name: accept an upload, store the bytes in an S3-compatible bucket, keep the description in MongoDB, and serve the file back by its id.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The same application lists and controls Docker containers, pings a Caddy server and can run commands over SSH. Plus a few other bits for the admin side.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That sounds like a lot of power. Who gets it?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Everything sits behind JWT login with three roles. Anyone signed in can download, moderators and admins can upload and manage containers, and only admins get the SSH command endpoint.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So roles decide what each person can touch.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Right. An upload checks the file extension, writes the bytes under a unique id, then records the metadata. A download reads that record, fetches the object and returns it with its type and size.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A compact backend with real range.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the API docs are served by Swagger. The full page lists every route.
